## Overview

Add opt-in MRv2 buffered dynamic PP for DeepSeek-V4 with local prefix reuse and a Mooncake cache-handoff backend. Movable layers keep independent cache pages; both stages agree on ownership after the previous owner finishes transferring their state.

This remains a **draft prototype**, pending human line-by-line review and NVIDIA model/native RDMA validation. Only vLLM is updated; [vllm-ascend#19868](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/19868) is unchanged. GitHub still reports base merge conflicts, already reported by a bot on October 27; this feature update does not rebase the PR.

## Claims

- Bounded activation snapshots, immutable boundary headers, and completed-device feedback support bounded movement of a PP2 boundary. Defaults retain fixed PP.
- Explicit local prefix support preserves central scheduler block IDs, hashes, sharing, eviction, reset and copy-on-write. Dedicated SWA, compressed KV, indexer and FP32 compressor pages include physical padding; both stages validate layout/group metadata.
- `dynamic_pp_config.kv_transfer_backend="mooncake"` reuses the **same engine initialization, registration/unregistration and batch synchronous WRITE implementation as MooncakeConnector**. PP owns its boundary epoch and cache lifetime; PD retains its existing request protocol. PP exchanges endpoints/addresses through its CPU group, without a PD router/bootstrap service or external `kv_transfer_config`.
- Both backends transfer complete state only when a layer changes owner, including cached prefixes of completed requests. Unchanged cuts copy no KV. Mooncake failures never commit ownership or silently fall back; failed writes retain buffers until worker exit. Normal shutdown unregisters before memory release.
- Separate eager DSV4 MTP1/OUT1 and MTP3 decode opt-ins remain guarded. Prefix/MTP3 shape windows accumulate cooldown across alternating batch shapes. Positive initial offsets account for the last stage's draft work.

**The current policy is full-state handoff.** Selecting Mooncake does not reduce copied bytes or provide asynchronous dirty-block replication. The user's proposed two-stage replicas with asynchronous initial/incremental updates are recorded as the next design direction, not implemented functionality.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| PP configuration/controller, real KVCacheManager and two-process Gloo | **121 passed** |
| Existing MooncakeConnector PD/HMA/hybrid-Mamba/statistics regression | **174 passed** |
| Non-type pre-commit checks and diff whitespace | Passed |
| Mypy, files touched in this update | 14 errors in existing GPU-worker/PD-connector code; identical error-message multiset on parent files, zero new errors |
| Native Mooncake TCP handoff | Added to dependency-equipped CI; not run locally |
| Real DSV4 CUDA prefix/registration test | Added/extended in optional B200 CI; not run locally |
| Forced-handoff CUDA/RDMA model accuracy and throughput | Pending; no result claimed |

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest -q \
  tests/v1/worker/test_pp_boundary.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_pp_buffer.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_pp_config.py
# 121 passed
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \
  -p pytest_asyncio.plugin -p tests.v1.kv_connector.unit.conftest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_stats.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hma.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py
# 174 passed (nine existing cleanup/coroutine warnings retained)
```

The local runner uses complete uv-cache copies of matching installed dependency versions because macOS offloaded environment files. Missing pytest-asyncio was installed only in a task-local directory, keeping the installed pytest version. The new PP tests use an **external Mooncake API double** that moves bytes through real Store messages between real processes; this is not native Mooncake/RDMA evidence. They prove completed/shared prefix reuse, padded-page COW, bidirectional handoff, reset/block reuse, backend/protocol mismatch rejection, paired startup/write failure handling, no ownership commit/fallback after failure, and explicit unregistration. The new backend regression fails on the parent state module because it has no Mooncake backend argument, then passes with the implementation.

No CUDA hardware or native Mooncake runtime is available locally; SSH155/156/159 timed out. The EC TCP CI job installs the matching CUDA wheel and now runs a native two-process CPU-memory Mooncake handoff test. The optional B200 DSV4 job installs Mooncake and adds a real prefix/cache-registration case; it does not force an ownership change. Stronger device-transfer accuracy and `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` validation remain pending. Earlier Ascend fresh-prefill/MTP results are not validation of this new native backend. The prior NVIDIA-model 34-error mypy baseline also remains documented; the current scoped 14-error comparison is separate.

## Details

Use eager MRv2 PP2, TP, chunked prefill disabled, `pp_send_buffer_size=2`, and `dynamic_pp_config.enabled=true`. For local prefix reuse also enable prefix caching plus `allow_prefix_caching=true`. `allow_mtp_prefill` permits eager MTP1/OUT1; `allow_mtp_decode` permits eager MTP3. Mooncake is selected with `kv_transfer_backend="mooncake"`, `mooncake_protocol` (default `"rdma"`; `"tcp"` for functional checks), and optional `mooncake_device_name`. The default cache transport remains `"collective"`. Missing native libraries fail setup instead of changing transports.

The engine registers movable allocations once and shares descriptors with the corresponding TP peer. Changed boundaries quiesce previous device work, execute the old-owner write, and propagate completion/error to both stages before advancing the epoch. This adds synchronization at an ownership change. Dedicated pages consume memory beyond the ordinary KV budget, with a full-size plus 1 GiB headroom check; automatic capacity accounting is pending. Large caches or frequent moves can be expensive. Resumed requests, external KV pooling/connectors, HiSparse, graphs, DP/EP/CP/SP, LoRA and cross-layer index reuse remain unsupported.

Shared transfer helpers live under the existing Mooncake connector package; PP epoch/replica logic stays under `vllm/v1/worker/pp/`. Rendered docs describe configuration, memory cost, transport lifetime and the distinction from continuous incremental replication.

Original duplicate-work checks found no equivalent runtime-boundary feedback design. Related #63106 supplies static DSV4.1 partitions and #41247 adjusts chunk sizes; Ascend #14945/#16618 use fold-back stages and MRv1 scheduling. The independent attention correctness fix remains [vllm-ascend#19864](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/19864).

AI assistance was used for implementation and validation. The human owner proposed and directed the design; human review and missing hardware evaluation are required before merge.

+# Experimental dynamic pipeline parallelism
+
+Dynamic pipeline parallelism moves a layer boundary between two pipeline
+stages for independent, complete prefills. Each stage loads a few overlapping
+layers. A bounded activation buffer lets a producer submit another batch while
+an earlier send is pending. Completed device timings and consumer credits then
+guide the boundary toward a balanced split.
+
+The feature is disabled by default and requires Model Runner V2. The initial
+model adapter is NVIDIA `DeepseekV4ForCausalLM`. Other models must implement
+`SupportsDynamicPP` before enabling boundary movement. Activation buffering
+without boundary movement can be enabled independently for MRv2 PP models.
+
+## Enable
+
+```bash
+VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
+    --pipeline-parallel-size 2 --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
+    --enforce-eager --no-enable-prefix-caching --no-enable-chunked-prefill \
+    --max-model-len 20992 --max-num-batched-tokens 20480 \
+    --additional-config '{
+      "pp_send_buffer_size": 2,
+      "dynamic_pp_config": {
+        "enabled": true,
+        "redundant_layers": 3,
+        "initial_offset": -3,
+        "high_watermark": 2,
+        "cooldown_steps": 8,
+        "log_interval_seconds": 10
+      }
+    }'
+```
+
+Send requests with `max_tokens=1`. Every prompt must fit in a single scheduled
+batch. An initial offset of -3 makes PP0 execute three fewer layers than its
+base partition. Later batches may move this boundary within the preloaded
+range. The active boundary is carried with each batch, so work already in
+flight continues to use its original split.
+
+To use activation buffering alone, set
+`--additional-config '{"pp_send_buffer_size": 2}'` without enabling
+`dynamic_pp_config`. This mode retains the model's fixed layer partition.
+
+## Configuration
+
+The following fields belong to `dynamic_pp_config`:
+
+| Field | Default | Meaning |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `enabled` | `false` | Enable boundary movement. |
+| `redundant_layers` | `2` | Load up to this many extra layers around the base boundary. |
+| `initial_offset` | `0` | Initial PP0 layer-count offset, within the redundant range. |
+| `adaptive` | `true` | Set `false` to hold the initial boundary for comparisons. |
+| `allow_mtp_prefill` | `false` | Opt into the restricted eager DeepSeek-V4 MTP1 fresh-prefill path described below. |
+| `allow_mtp_decode` | `false` | Opt into eager DeepSeek-V4 MTP3 with isolated cache state and acknowledged ownership handoff. |
+| `allow_prefix_caching` | `false` | Enable local prefix reuse with dedicated movable-layer cache pages and ownership handoff. |
+| `kv_transfer_backend` | `"collective"` | Cache handoff transport: `"collective"` or MooncakeConnector's `"mooncake"` memory transport. |
+| `mooncake_protocol` | `"rdma"` | Mooncake transport protocol; `"tcp"` is also useful for functional checks. |
+| `mooncake_device_name` | `""` | Optional Mooncake device filter, with the same meaning as in MooncakeConnector. |
+| `low_watermark` | `0` | Low completed-activation queue depth. |
+| `high_watermark` | `2` | High completed-activation queue depth; must exceed the low watermark. |
+| `cooldown_steps` | `8` | Matching completed timing samples required before a move. |
+| `max_step` | `1` | Maximum layers moved in one decision. |
+| `balance_tolerance_percent` | `3` | Hold when stage times differ by no more than this percentage. |
+| `feedback_timeout_seconds` | `30` | Hold the boundary when consumer feedback becomes stale. |
+| `log_interval_seconds` | `10` | Periodic strategy logging; `0` disables it. |
+
+`pp_send_buffer_size` defaults to `0`. A positive value reserves that many
+independent activation snapshots before memory profiling determines the KV
+budget. Dynamic mode requires a capacity at least as large as the high
+watermark. More slots and overlapping weights consume additional device memory.
+Snapshots also add a device copy per inter-stage output.
+
+## Feedback and observation
+
+The queue depth is completed producer work minus credited consumer starts.
+Posted communication handles are reported separately and never count as ready
+activations. TP0 polls device events and exchanges bounded snapshots through
+the existing PP CPU store; the hot path does not read a device tensor on the
+host or synchronize the device for timing. TP0 broadcasts each decision within
+its tensor-parallel group.
+
+The controller matches timings by batch, boundary version, token count, and
+request count. It uses a median window, ignores stale versions, and holds
+within a tolerance. Watermarks shorten the confirmation window when they agree
+with the timing imbalance. When credits lag, sustained timing evidence can
+still trigger a move. Previously measured neighboring cuts prevent repeated
+oscillation between integer layer counts; changes in device load invalidate
+incomparable costs.
+
+`Dynamic PP strategy` logs show both execution ranges, boundary version,
+completed queue depth, stage times, decision reason, and the splits used during
+the reporting interval. A stable boundary with `balanced_hold`, or an adjacent
+cut that is no faster, identifies a candidate steady-state split for that
+workload. It is not a universal partition for other prompt or batch sizes.
+
+## Current limits
+
+The default boundary path supports eager PP=2, TP, complete fresh prefills, and one
+output token per request. Prefix caching, chunked prefill, decode, KV
+connectors, speculative verification, LoRA, DP, EP, context parallelism, sequence parallel
+MoE, microbatching, and cross-layer index reuse are rejected. PP buffering
+does not support sleep mode or the external launcher.
+
+Speculative configuration is rejected by default. The experimental
+`allow_mtp_prefill=true` opt-in permits only DeepSeek-V4 with
+`--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1,"enforce_eager":true}'`.
+It retains the complete fresh-prefill and `max_tokens=1` checks, and rejects
+scheduled verification tokens. The platform adapter must isolate the PP=1
+draft's configuration and MoE execution context from the target pipeline.
+This is a prefill/TTFT probe: draft work can add last-stage cost even for OUT1,
+but it does not establish verification, acceptance-rate, or decode support.
+
+The default prefill path does not allocate movable-layer KV replicas. Fresh prefills compute each
+logical layer exactly once and finish before historical KV can be needed.
+Supporting cached prefixes or subsequent chunks requires consistent cache
+ownership and updates on every rank that might execute those layers. Disabling
+prefix caching alone does not make chunked prefill or decode safe.
+
+### Experimental MTP3 state handoff
+
+`allow_mtp_decode=true` is a separate opt-in for DeepSeek-V4 with eager MTP and
+exactly three speculative tokens. It cannot be combined with `allow_mtp_prefill`.
+The model adapter must allocate independent complete backing for every movable
+layer's attention, compressed, indexer, and compressor state. Copies include
+physical page padding and indexer scales. Shared cache pools cannot be copied
+as if they were independent layer state.
+
+Before either stage executes a batch, PP0 acquires its activation-send slot
+and publishes its boundary to the PP CPU-group Store. PP1 consumes and deletes
+the header before receiving that batch. Completed metadata sends bound unconsumed
+headers by the ring capacity. PP0 does not wait for PP1 on an unchanged cut.
+On an ownership change both stages finish prior device work,
+transfer every changed layer's complete state from its previous owner, and
+wait for completion. The activation header must match this control epoch.
+Unchanged boundaries copy no KV and add no device synchronization or two-way
+PP control rendezvous. Each batch still publishes and consumes one small header. Stage feedback includes the
+last stage's MTP proposals; ownership-transfer time is reported separately and
+remains part of end-to-end latency.
+
+This path assumes the central KV planner's common group/block mapping and
+checks matching component shapes, types, byte counts, and independent storage.
+It does not add pooled KV, resumed requests, chunking, or graphs. Local prefix
+reuse requires the additional opt-in below.
+Independent state requires memory beyond the ordinary KV budget; the adapter
+must check capacity before allocating it. This complete-state handoff is an
+experimental implementation, not an incremental background KV replication path.
+
+### Local prefix caching
+
+Enable `--enable-prefix-caching` together with
+`"allow_prefix_caching": true` in `dynamic_pp_config`. Keep eager execution,
+PP=2, and chunked prefill disabled. This opt-in is supported by the NVIDIA
+DeepSeek-V4 adapter, for OUT1 prefills or together with `allow_mtp_decode` for
+MTP3 decode. The restricted MTP1 prefill mode can also reuse local prefixes;
+its one-output-token limit remains in force. KV connectors and HiSparse are
+not supported. A platform adapter must implement both cache-state and
+cache-layout accessors before using this opt-in.
+
+The scheduler continues to own prefix hashes, reference counts, eviction,
+and physical block IDs. A cache hit executes the **entire uncached suffix**
+in one batch, including the last prompt token on a full-prefix match.
+Partial suffix scheduling and resumed requests are rejected.
+
+Each movable component gets independent, padded cache pages before binding.
+This includes SWA, compressed KV, indexer bytes/scales, and FP32 compressor
+state. Scheduler block IDs and kernel view shapes stay the same. The normal
+copy-on-write and block-zeroing paths operate on these views, including raw
+page padding. Nonmovable layers keep their ordinary pooled allocation.
+
+Both PP stages check the movable components' scheduler group IDs, cache
+specifications, block count, kernel block sizes, view strides, hit alignment,
+hash block size, and retention policy before the first real batch. A mismatch
+aborts instead of reading another group's blocks. When a layer changes owner,
+the handoff copies **every physical block** of that layer, including reusable
+prefixes belonging to completed requests. No copy is needed on an unchanged
+cut. Prefix-cache reset and eviction keep their scheduler semantics; the
+runtime does not create a second hash index or invalidate hits on each move.
+
+Dedicated pages consume memory beyond the ordinary KV pool. Allocation checks
+their complete size plus 1 GiB device headroom. Use a conservative explicit
+`--kv-cache-memory-bytes` budget for this prototype; the extra storage is not
+yet integrated into the scheduler's automatic KV capacity calculation.
+Ownership changes quiesce both stages and transfer complete state, so a large
+cache can make frequent moves expensive. This is local prefix reuse with
+ownership handoff, not background incremental replication or pooled KV import.
+
+For MTP workloads, start with a **positive** `initial_offset` (for example `2`)
+to give PP0 more target layers: PP1 also runs the draft steps. The feedback
+measures that last-stage draft work and can adjust the split further.
+
+### Mooncake transport for ownership handoff
+
+Set `kv_transfer_backend` to `"mooncake"` alongside prefix caching or MTP3
+decode. Install the platform-compatible Mooncake package from
+`requirements/kv_connectors.txt` first; CUDA 13 installations need the
+corresponding `mooncake-transfer-engine-cuda13` wheel. Missing libraries or
+initialization failures abort setup; the runtime never silently substitutes
+the collective backend.
+
+For example, merge these fields into `dynamic_pp_config` for local prefix reuse:
+
+```json
+{
+  "enabled": true,
+  "allow_prefix_caching": true,
+  "kv_transfer_backend": "mooncake",
+  "mooncake_protocol": "rdma",
+  "redundant_layers": 2,
+  "initial_offset": 2
+}
+```
+
+Keep `pp_send_buffer_size=2`, eager PP2, and `--enable-prefix-caching`.
+Do not configure a PD `kv_transfer_config`: this is internal PP ownership,
+and external KV connectors remain unsupported. PP and MooncakeConnector share
+the engine initialization, memory registration/unregistration, and synchronous
+batch-write implementation under `mooncake/transfer_engine.py`. The engine uses
+`P2PHANDSHAKE`; PP exchanges registered addresses through its existing CPU
+group, so a PD bootstrap service, router, or request-release protocol is not
+required.
+
+Each worker registers its dedicated movable cache allocations once. On a cut
+change, the old owner writes the changed layers to its matching TP peer. Both
+stages agree on transfer completion before committing the ownership epoch.
+Writes include all state bytes and padding. A failed write poisons the runtime:
+neither stage commits the new epoch or falls back to another transport, and
+buffers remain alive until worker exit. Normal shutdown unregisters memory
+before releasing allocations. Unchanged cuts perform no Mooncake operation.
+
+This selects the transport for **full-state handoff**. It does not yet send
+only valid or dirty blocks, continuously synchronize replicas, or overlap
+replication with inference. In particular, selecting Mooncake alone does not
+reduce the number of bytes copied. Native TCP and CUDA/RDMA validation are
+separate from protocol unit tests with an external engine double.
+
+Balancing can reduce bubbles caused by unequal stage times. Startup, drain,
+communication, and the indivisibility of layers still impose limits. Measure
+end-to-end throughput and latency with the intended workload before drawing a
+performance conclusion.

+class LayerChain(torch.nn.Module):
+    def __init__(self, rank, device):
+        super().__init__()

+                )
+            }
+        )
+
+    def forward(self, value):
+        start, end = self.execution_range

+def select_pp_moe_layer_names(
+    layer_names: Sequence[str], layer_prefix: str, start: int, end: int
+) -> list[str]:
+    """Order fast-MoE dispatch by this batch's executed logical layers."""
+    prefix = f"{layer_prefix}."
+    by_layer: dict[int, list[str]] = {}
+    for name in layer_names:
+        if not name.startswith(prefix):
+            continue
+        index, separator, _ = name[len(prefix) :].partition(".")
+        if separator and index.isdecimal():
+            by_layer.setdefault(int(index), []).append(name)
+    missing = [index for index in range(start, end) if index not in by_layer]
+    if missing:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"Missing dynamic PP MoE dispatch entries for layers {missing}"
+        )
+    return [name for index in range(start, end) for name in by_layer[index]]

+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class DynamicPPConfig:
+    enabled: bool = False
+    redundant_layers: int = 2
+    initial_offset: int = 0
+    adaptive: bool = True
+    allow_mtp_prefill: bool = False
+    allow_mtp_decode: bool = False
+    allow_prefix_caching: bool = False
+    kv_transfer_backend: str = "collective"
+    mooncake_protocol: str = "rdma"
+    mooncake_device_name: str = ""
+    low_watermark: int = 0
+    high_watermark: int = 2
+    cooldown_steps: int = 8
+    max_step: int = 1
+    log_interval_seconds: int = 10
+    balance_tolerance_percent: int = 3
+    feedback_timeout_seconds: int = 30
+
+    @classmethod
+    def from_mapping(cls, value: Mapping[str, Any] | None) -> "DynamicPPConfig":
+        if value is None:
+            return cls()
+        if not isinstance(value, Mapping):
+            raise ValueError("dynamic_pp_config must be an object")
+        unknown = value.keys() - {item.name for item in fields(cls)}
+        if unknown:
+            raise ValueError(f"Unknown dynamic_pp_config fields: {sorted(unknown)}")
+        result = cls(**value)
+        for item in fields(cls):
+            expected = (
+                bool
+                if item.name
+                in (
+                    "enabled",
+                    "adaptive",
+                    "allow_mtp_prefill",
+                    "allow_mtp_decode",
+                    "allow_prefix_caching",
+                )
+                else str
+                if item.name
+                in ("kv_transfer_backend", "mooncake_protocol", "mooncake_device_name")
+                else int
+            )
+            if type(getattr(result, item.name)) is not expected:
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"dynamic_pp_config.{item.name} must be {expected.__name__}"
+                )
+        if result.kv_transfer_backend not in ("collective", "mooncake"):
+            raise ValueError("Dynamic PP KV backend must be collective or mooncake")
+        if not result.mooncake_protocol:
+            raise ValueError("Dynamic PP Mooncake protocol must not be empty")
+        if (
+            result.redundant_layers < 1
+            or result.max_step < 1
+            or result.cooldown_steps < 1
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Dynamic PP redundancy, max_step, and cooldown_steps must be positive"
+            )
+        if not 0 <= result.low_watermark < result.high_watermark:
+            raise ValueError("Dynamic PP requires 0 <= low_watermark < high_watermark")
+        if abs(result.initial_offset) > result.redundant_layers:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Dynamic PP initial_offset exceeds the redundant layer range"
+            )
+        if result.log_interval_seconds < 0:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Dynamic PP log interval must be non-negative (0 disables logging)"
+            )
+        if (
+            not 0 <= result.balance_tolerance_percent < 100
+            or result.feedback_timeout_seconds < 1
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Dynamic PP needs tolerance in [0, 100) and a positive feedback timeout"
+            )
+        return result
+
+    def validate_runtime(self, vllm_config: Any, buffer_size: int) -> None:
+        if buffer_size and not vllm_config.use_v2_model_runner:
+            raise ValueError("pp_send_buffer_size requires Model Runner V2")
+        if not self.enabled:
+            return
+        if self.kv_transfer_backend == "mooncake" and not (
+            self.allow_mtp_decode
+            or (
+                self.allow_prefix_caching
+                and vllm_config.cache_config.enable_prefix_caching
+            )
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("Dynamic PP Mooncake needs prefix caching or MTP decode")
+        parallel = vllm_config.parallel_config
+        model = vllm_config.model_config
+        if not vllm_config.use_v2_model_runner or parallel.pipeline_parallel_size != 2:
+            raise ValueError("Dynamic PP currently requires Model Runner V2 and PP=2")
+        if not model.enforce_eager:
+            raise ValueError("Dynamic PP currently requires eager execution")
+        if buffer_size < self.high_watermark:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "pp_send_buffer_size must be at least the dynamic PP high_watermark"
+            )
+        if (
+            parallel.data_parallel_size != 1
+            or parallel.enable_expert_parallel
+            or parallel.use_sequence_parallel_moe
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Dynamic PP does not yet support DP, EP, or sequence parallel MoE"
+            )
+        if (
+            parallel.prefill_context_parallel_size != 1
+            or parallel.decode_context_parallel_size != 1
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("Dynamic PP does not yet support context parallelism")
+        if vllm_config.kv_transfer_config is not None:
+            raise ValueError("Dynamic PP does not yet support KV connectors")
+        speculative = vllm_config.speculative_config
+        if self.allow_mtp_prefill and self.allow_mtp_decode:
+            raise ValueError("Choose either MTP prefill or state-migrating decode")
+        if speculative is not None and not (
+            self.allow_mtp_prefill or self.allow_mtp_decode
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Dynamic PP speculation requires allow_mtp_prefill or allow_mtp_decode"
+            )
+        if self.allow_mtp_prefill and (
+            speculative is None
+            or getattr(model.hf_config, "model_type", None) != "deepseek_v4"
+            or speculative.method != "mtp"
+            or speculative.num_speculative_tokens != 1
+            or speculative.enforce_eager is not True
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Dynamic PP allow_mtp_prefill requires DeepSeek-V4 with eager "
+                "MTP and exactly one speculative token"
+            )
+        if self.allow_mtp_decode and (
+            speculative is None
+            or getattr(model.hf_config, "model_type", None) != "deepseek_v4"
+            or speculative.method != "mtp"
+            or speculative.num_speculative_tokens != 3
+            or speculative.enforce_eager is not True
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Dynamic PP allow_mtp_decode requires DeepSeek-V4 with eager "
+                "MTP and exactly three speculative tokens"
+            )
+        if (
+            vllm_config.cache_config.enable_prefix_caching
+            and not self.allow_prefix_caching
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Dynamic PP prefix caching requires KV replicas; "
+                "opt in with allow_prefix_caching"
+            )
+        if self.allow_prefix_caching and (
+            getattr(model.hf_config, "model_type", None) != "deepseek_v4"
+            or vllm_config.attention_config.hisparse_config is not None
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Dynamic PP prefix caching requires the DeepSeek-V4 cache adapter "
+                "without HiSparse"
+            )
+        if getattr(vllm_config, "lora_config", None) is not None:
+            raise ValueError("Dynamic PP does not yet support LoRA")
+        if parallel.use_ubatching:
+            raise ValueError("Dynamic PP does not yet support microbatching")
+        if vllm_config.scheduler_config.enable_chunked_prefill:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Dynamic PP currently requires chunked prefill to be disabled"
+            )
+        hf_config = model.hf_config
+        if getattr(hf_config, "use_index_cache", False) or "shared" in (
+            getattr(hf_config, "indexer_types", ()) or ()
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("Dynamic PP does not yet support cross-layer index reuse")

+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class PPBoundary:
+    batch_id: int
+    boundary: int
+    version: int
+
+    def to_wire(self) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
+        return self.batch_id, self.boundary, self.version
+
+    @classmethod
+    def from_wire(cls, value: Any) -> "PPBoundary":
+        if (
+            not isinstance(value, (tuple, list))
+            or len(value) != 3
+            or any(type(item) is not int for item in value)
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("Invalid dynamic PP batch header")
+        if value[0] < 0 or value[2] < 0:
+            raise ValueError("Dynamic PP batch and version must be non-negative")

+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class PPBalanceSample:
+    batch_id: int
+    boundary: int
+    version: int
+    num_tokens: int
+    num_reqs: int
+    pp0_ms: float
+    pp1_ms: float
+

+class PPBoundaryController:
+    """Move one PP2 boundary within its preloaded layer range."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        config: DynamicPPConfig,
+        base_boundary: int,
+        num_layers: int,
+        minimum_boundary: int = 1,
+    ):
+        if not 0 < base_boundary < num_layers:
+            raise ValueError("Dynamic PP needs two non-empty base stages")
+        self.config = config
+        self.base_boundary = base_boundary
+        self.num_layers = num_layers
+        self.minimum = max(1, minimum_boundary, base_boundary - config.redundant_layers)
+        self.maximum = min(num_layers - 1, base_boundary + config.redundant_layers)
+        self.boundary = base_boundary + config.initial_offset
+        if not self.minimum <= self.boundary <= self.maximum:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Dynamic PP initial boundary violates stage or hash-routing limits"
+            )
+        self.version = 0
+        self._samples: deque[PPBalanceSample] = deque(maxlen=config.cooldown_steps)
+        self._retain_shape_windows = (
+            config.allow_mtp_decode or config.allow_prefix_caching
+        )
+        self._decode_windows: OrderedDict[
+            tuple[int, int], tuple[deque[PPBalanceSample], int]
+        ] = OrderedDict()
+        self._last_sample_batch = -1
+        self._samples_since_change = 0
+        self._costs: dict[tuple[int, int, int], tuple[float, float]] = {}
+        self.feedback_stats: dict[str, Any] = {"decision": "awaiting_completed_samples"}
+        self._last_batch_id = -1
+        self._last_received_version = -1
+        self._last_received_boundary: int | None = None
+
+    def loaded_range(self, rank: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
+        if rank == 0:
+            return 0, self.maximum
+        if rank == 1:
+            return self.minimum, self.num_layers
+        raise ValueError("Dynamic PP currently supports only ranks 0 and 1")
+
+    def execution_range(self, rank: int, header: PPBoundary) -> tuple[int, int]:
+        if not self.minimum <= header.boundary <= self.maximum:
+            raise ValueError("Dynamic PP batch boundary is outside the preloaded range")
+        if rank == 0:
+            return 0, header.boundary
+        if rank == 1:
+            return header.boundary, self.num_layers
+        raise ValueError("Dynamic PP currently supports only ranks 0 and 1")
+
+    def choose(
+        self,
+        batch_id: int,
+        queue_depth: int,
+        samples: Sequence[PPBalanceSample] = (),
+        feedback_fresh: bool = True,
+    ) -> PPBoundary:
+        if batch_id <= self._last_batch_id or queue_depth < 0:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Dynamic PP needs increasing batch ids and non-negative queue depth"
+            )
+        self._last_batch_id = batch_id
+        if self.feedback_stats.get("feedback_version") != self.version:
+            self.feedback_stats.clear()
+        added = False
+        for sample in samples:
+            if sample.batch_id >= batch_id:
+                raise ValueError("Dynamic PP feedback cannot refer to a future batch")
+            if not all(
+                isfinite(value) and value > 0
+                for value in (sample.pp0_ms, sample.pp1_ms)
+            ):
+                raise ValueError("Dynamic PP stage times must be finite and positive")
+            if sample.batch_id <= self._last_sample_batch:
+                continue
+            self._last_sample_batch = sample.batch_id
+            # Queued old work must not drive the new boundary again.
+            if (sample.boundary, sample.version) != (self.boundary, self.version):
+                continue
+            shape = sample.num_tokens, sample.num_reqs
+            if self._retain_shape_windows:
+                previous_shape = (
+                    (self._samples[-1].num_tokens, self._samples[-1].num_reqs)
+                    if self._samples
+                    else None
+                )
+                self._samples, self._samples_since_change = self._decode_windows.pop(
+                    shape, (deque(maxlen=self.config.cooldown_steps), 0)
+                )
+                if shape != previous_shape:
+                    self.feedback_stats.clear()
+            elif self._samples and shape != (
+                self._samples[-1].num_tokens,
+                self._samples[-1].num_reqs,
+            ):
+                self._samples.clear()
+                self._samples_since_change = 0
+                self.feedback_stats.clear()
+            self._samples.append(sample)
+            self._samples_since_change += 1
+            if self._retain_shape_windows:
+                self._decode_windows[shape] = (
+                    self._samples,
+                    self._samples_since_change,
+                )
+                if len(self._decode_windows) > DECODE_TIMING_WINDOW_LIMIT:
+                    self._decode_windows.popitem(last=False)
+            added = True
+        self.feedback_stats.update(
+            feedback_version=self.version,
+            matched_samples=len(self._samples),
+            completed_samples_since_change=self._samples_since_change,
+            ready_queue_depth=queue_depth,
+        )
+        if not self.config.adaptive:
+            self.feedback_stats["decision"] = "fixed_boundary"
+        elif not feedback_fresh:
+            self.feedback_stats["decision"] = "stale_feedback_hold"
+            self._clear_timing_windows()
+            self.feedback_stats["matched_samples"] = 0
+            self.feedback_stats["completed_samples_since_change"] = 0
+        elif len(self._samples) < self.config.cooldown_steps:
+            self.feedback_stats["decision"] = "awaiting_completed_samples"
+        elif added:
+            self._rebalance(queue_depth)
+        return PPBoundary(batch_id, self.boundary, self.version)
+
+    def _clear_timing_windows(self) -> None:
+        self._samples.clear()
+        self._samples_since_change = 0
+        self._decode_windows.clear()
+
+    def _rebalance(self, queue_depth: int) -> None:
+        first = self._samples[-1]
+        pp0_ms = median(sample.pp0_ms for sample in self._samples)
+        pp1_ms = median(sample.pp1_ms for sample in self._samples)
+        cost = max(pp0_ms, pp1_ms)
+        imbalance = (pp0_ms - pp1_ms) / cost
+        tolerance = self.config.balance_tolerance_percent / 100
+        key = (self.boundary, first.num_tokens, first.num_reqs)
+        reference = self._costs.get(key)
+        if reference is not None and any(
+            abs(current - old) / old > COST_HISTORY_DRIFT_MULTIPLIER * tolerance
+            for current, old in zip((pp0_ms, pp1_ms), reference)
+        ):
+            # An old neighboring cut is no longer comparable after device
+            # load changes. Keep an anchor rather than refreshing it every
+            # batch, so gradual drift is detected too.
+            self._costs = {k: v for k, v in self._costs.items() if k[1:] != key[1:]}
+        self._costs.setdefault(key, (pp0_ms, pp1_ms))
+        self.feedback_stats.update(
+            pp0_device_ms=round(pp0_ms, 3),
+            pp1_device_ms=round(pp1_ms, 3),
+            imbalance_percent=round(imbalance * 100, 3),
+            timing_batch_id=first.batch_id,
+            timing_num_tokens=first.num_tokens,
+            timing_num_reqs=first.num_reqs,
+        )
+        if abs(imbalance) <= tolerance:
+            self.feedback_stats["decision"] = "balanced_hold"
+            return

+            "watermark_kind": "device_ready_minus_consumer_credit",
+            "pending_send_count": pending_sends,

+            "window_pending_send_max": self._pending_max,
+            "balance_feedback": dict(self.controller.feedback_stats)
+            if self.pp_rank == 0

+            self._pending_min = self._pending_max = None

+"""Bounded snapshots of PP outputs whose sends may outlive the next forward."""
+
+from collections import deque
+from collections.abc import Callable, Mapping, Sequence
+from contextlib import nullcontext
+from copy import deepcopy
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from typing import Any, Protocol
+
+import torch
+
+
+class SendWork(Protocol):
+    def is_completed(self) -> bool: ...
+
+    def wait(self) -> None: ...
+
+
+@dataclass
+class _SendSlot:
+    buffers: dict[str, torch.Tensor] = field(default_factory=dict)
+    payload: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
+    works: Sequence[SendWork] = ()
+
+
+class PPSendBuffer:
+    """Keep independent output storage until the matching send has completed.
+
+    ``acquire`` runs before forward and only waits when all slots are busy.
+    ``send`` snapshots on the producer stream, then posts communication on a
+    separate stream. Keeping a reference to a graph output alone is unsafe:
+    the next replay may overwrite the same allocation.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self, capacity: int, device_module: Any = None, *, metadata_handles: int = 0
+    ):
+        if type(capacity) is not int or capacity < 1:
+            raise ValueError("PP send buffer capacity must be a positive integer")
+        self._metadata_handles = metadata_handles
+        self.capacity = capacity
+        self._device_module = device_module
+        self._comm_stream = (
+            device_module.Stream() if device_module is not None else None
+        )
+        self._slots = [_SendSlot() for _ in range(capacity)]
+        self._free = deque(range(capacity))
+        self._pending: deque[int] = deque()
+        self._active: int | None = None
+        self._reserved = False
+        self._failure: Exception | None = None
+        self.num_backpressure_waits = 0
+        self.num_sends = 0
+
+    @property
+    def reserved_bytes(self) -> int:
+        return sum(
+            t.numel() * t.element_size()
+            for slot in self._slots
+            for t in slot.buffers.values()
+        )
+
+    @property
+    def pending_count(self) -> int:
+        """Posted sends, including transfers that may already be complete."""
+        self._reap_completed()
+        return len(self._pending)
+
+    def reserve(self, tensors: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
+        """Allocate maximum output storage before the KV memory budget is set."""
+        if self._pending or self._active is not None:
+            raise RuntimeError("Cannot reserve PP output storage while it is in use")
+        for slot in self._slots:
+            slot.buffers = {
+                key: torch.empty_like(value, memory_format=torch.contiguous_format)
+                for key, value in tensors.items()
+                if isinstance(value, torch.Tensor)
+            }
+        self._reserved = True
+
+    def _check_failure(self) -> None:
+        if self._failure is not None:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                "PP send buffer cannot be reused after a communication failure"
+            ) from self._failure
+
+    def _finish_oldest(self) -> None:
+        index = self._pending[0]
+        slot = self._slots[index]
+        try:
+            # Device work waits order subsequent slot writes on the caller's
+            # stream. CPU metadata buffers must also remain alive until done.
+            for work in slot.works:
+                work.wait()
+        except Exception as error:
+            self._failure = error
+            raise
+        slot.works = ()
+        slot.payload = {}
+        self._pending.popleft()
+        self._free.append(index)
+
+    def _reap_completed(self) -> None:
+        self._check_failure()
+        while self._pending:
+            slot = self._slots[self._pending[0]]
+            # GroupCoordinator retains Gloo metadata separately. Its Work
+            # does not reliably report completion until wait() is called.
+            if not all(
+                work.is_completed() for work in slot.works[self._metadata_handles :]
+            ):
+                break
+            self._finish_oldest()
+
+    def acquire(self) -> None:
+        """Reserve a slot before starting a forward that can produce output."""
+        self._check_failure()
+        if self._active is not None:
+            raise RuntimeError("A PP output slot has already been acquired")
+        self._reap_completed()
+        if not self._free:
+            self.num_backpressure_waits += 1
+            self._finish_oldest()
+        self._active = self._free.popleft()
+
+    def cancel(self) -> None:
+        """Release a reservation when this step produces no PP output."""
+        if self._active is not None:
+            self._free.appendleft(self._active)
+            self._active = None
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _view(buffer: torch.Tensor, value: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor | None:
+        if buffer.device != value.device or buffer.dtype != value.dtype:
+            return None
+        if buffer.shape == value.shape:
+            return buffer
+        if (
+            value.ndim
+            and buffer.ndim == value.ndim
+            and buffer.shape[1:] == value.shape[1:]
+            and buffer.shape[0] >= value.shape[0]
+        ):
+            return buffer[: value.shape[0]]
+        return None
+
+    def send(
+        self,
+        tensors: Mapping[str, Any],
+        send_fn: Callable[[dict[str, Any]], Sequence[SendWork]],
+        on_snapshot: Callable[[], None] | None = None,
+    ) -> None:
+        self._check_failure()
+        if self._active is None:
+            raise RuntimeError("Acquire a PP output slot before sending")
+        index = self._active
+        slot = self._slots[index]
+        payload: dict[str, Any] = {}
+        for key, value in tensors.items():
+            if not isinstance(value, torch.Tensor):
+                payload[key] = deepcopy(value)
+                continue
+            buffer = slot.buffers.get(key)
+            view = None if buffer is None else self._view(buffer, value)
+            if view is None:
+                if self._reserved:
+                    raise ValueError(
+                        f"PP tensor {key!r} exceeds its reserved output storage"
+                    )
+                slot.buffers[key] = torch.empty_like(
+                    value, memory_format=torch.contiguous_format
+                )
+                view = slot.buffers[key]
+            payload[key] = view.copy_(value)
+
+        slot.payload = payload
+        if on_snapshot is not None:
+            on_snapshot()
+        context = nullcontext()
+        if self._device_module is not None:
+            assert self._comm_stream is not None
+            self._comm_stream.wait_stream(self._device_module.current_stream())
+            context = self._device_module.stream(self._comm_stream)
+        try:
+            with context:
+                slot.works = tuple(send_fn(payload))
+        except Exception as error:
+            # A failed post may have issued some transfers. Keep its storage
+            # alive and prevent further reuse rather than guessing completion.
+            self._failure = error
+            raise
+        self._pending.append(index)
+        self._active = None
+        self.num_sends += 1
+
+    def drain(self) -> None:
+        """Finish all sends before shutdown, sleep, or releasing the buffers."""
+        self._check_failure()
+        self.cancel()
+        while self._pending:
+            self._finish_oldest()

+"""Dedicated movable-layer cache pages with scheduler block IDs unchanged."""
+
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+from typing import Any
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import (
+    KVCacheConfig,
+    KVCacheTensor,
+    UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs,
+    create_kv_cache_views,
+)

+
+def isolate_pp_cache(
+    config: KVCacheConfig,
+    caches: dict[str, torch.Tensor],
+    components: Mapping[str, tuple[int, str]],
+    layout: KVCacheLayout,
+    kernel_block_sizes: list[int],
+    device: torch.device,
+) -> tuple[dict[int, dict[str, torch.Tensor]], dict[int, dict[str, Any]]]:
+    """Allocate before binding or inference; never clone a shared pool per layer.
+
+    Each component gets complete, padded pages for every scheduler block ID,
+    including cached blocks with no live request. Other layers retain their
+    original pooled storage. Allocation failures leave the input views intact.
+    """
+    if not components:
+        raise ValueError("Dynamic PP requires movable cache components")
+    plans = []
+    identities = set()
+    for name, (layer, key) in sorted(components.items()):
+        if name not in caches or (layer, key) in identities:
+            raise ValueError(f"Missing or duplicate dynamic PP cache component {name}")
+        identities.add((layer, key))
+        matches = [
+            (i, group)
+            for i, group in enumerate(config.kv_cache_groups)
+            if name in group.layer_names
+        ]
+        if len(matches) != 1:
+            raise ValueError(f"Dynamic PP cache {name} needs one scheduler group")
+        group_id, group = matches[0]
+        spec = group.kv_cache_spec
+        if isinstance(spec, UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs):
+            spec = spec.kv_cache_specs[name]
+        if group.host_resident or not spec.has_layer_views or spec.num_heads != 1:
+            raise ValueError("Dynamic PP requires device cache pages with layer views")
+        size = config.num_blocks * spec.page_size_bytes
+        tensor = KVCacheTensor(
+            size=size,
+            layers=[name],
+            layer_stride=size,
+            block_stride=spec.page_size_bytes,
+        )
+        kernel_size = kernel_block_sizes[group_id]
+        description = (
+            group_id,
+            repr(spec),
+            config.num_blocks,
+            kernel_size,
+            layout.name,
+            config.hash_block_size,
+            config.cache_hit_alignment_tokens,
+            config.prefix_cache_retention_interval,
+            group.is_eagle_group,
+        )
+        plans.append((name, layer, key, spec, tensor, kernel_size, description))
+
+    required = sum(plan[4].size for plan in plans)
+    if device.type == "cuda":
+        free, _ = torch.accelerator.get_memory_info(device)
+        if free < required + (1 << 30):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"Dynamic PP needs {required} extra cache bytes plus 1 GiB headroom"
+            )
+    state: dict[int, dict[str, torch.Tensor]] = {}
+    descriptions: dict[int, dict[str, Any]] = {}
+    views = {}
+    for name, layer, key, spec, tensor, kernel_size, description in plans:
+        raw = torch.zeros(tensor.size, dtype=torch.int8, device=device)
+        view = create_kv_cache_views(
+            raw,
+            spec,
+            config.num_blocks,
+            layout,
+            tensor,
+            kernel_block_size=kernel_size,
+        )[0]
+        if view.shape != caches[name].shape or view.dtype != caches[name].dtype:
+            raise ValueError(f"Dynamic PP cache view changed shape or dtype: {name}")
+        views[name] = view
+        state.setdefault(layer, {})[key] = raw
+        descriptions.setdefault(layer, {})[key] = (
+            description,
+            tuple(view.shape),
+            tuple(view.stride()),
+            str(view.dtype),
+        )
+    caches.update(views)
+    return state, descriptions
+
+
+def prepare_pp_cache(
+    config: KVCacheConfig,
+    caches: dict[str, torch.Tensor],
+    forward_context: Mapping[str, Any],
+    layout: KVCacheLayout,
+    kernel_block_sizes: list[int],
+    device: torch.device,
+) -> None:
+    components = {
+        name: layer.dynamic_pp_cache_component
+        for name, layer in forward_context.items()
+        if hasattr(layer, "dynamic_pp_cache_component")
+    }
+    state, descriptions = isolate_pp_cache(
+        config, caches, components, layout, kernel_block_sizes, device
+    )
+    for name, (layer, key) in components.items():
+        forward_context[name].dynamic_pp_cache_raw = state[layer][key]
+        forward_context[name].dynamic_pp_cache_layout = descriptions[layer][key]

+        """Model pre-hook: on PP1 this follows receive and input copies."""
+        if self._active is not None:
+            self._active.start.record()
+            self._active.started = True
+
+    def finish(self) -> None:
+        """PP0: after output snapshot; PP1: after logits and sampling."""
+        step = self._active
+        if step is None:
+            return
+        if not step.started:
+            raise RuntimeError("Dynamic PP model start event was not recorded")
+        step.end.record()
+        self._steps.append(step)
+        self._active = None
+        self.poll()
+
+    def _publish(self) -> None:
+        self.store.set(
+            FEEDBACK_KEY,
+            json.dumps(
+                {
+                    "sequence": self._sequence,
+                    "consumed_batch_id": self.consumed_batch_id,
+                    "samples": [asdict(sample) for sample in self._samples],
+                }
+            ),
+        )
+
+    def poll(self) -> None:
+        changed = False
+        while self._steps:
+            step = self._steps[0]
+            if (
+                self.pp_rank == 1
+                and step.start.query()
+                and step.header.batch_id > self.consumed_batch_id
+            ):
+                self.consumed_batch_id = step.header.batch_id
+                changed = True
+            if not step.end.query():
+                break
+            self._steps.popleft()
+            if self.pp_rank == 0:
+                self.ready_batch_id = step.header.batch_id
+            self._samples.append(
+                PPStageSample(
+                    step.header.batch_id,
+                    step.header.boundary,
+                    step.header.version,
+                    step.num_tokens,
+                    step.num_reqs,
+                    step.start.elapsed_time(step.end),
+                )
+            )
+            changed = True
+        if self.pp_rank == 1:
+            if changed:
+                self._sequence += 1
+                self._publish()
+            return
+        # check() never waits for the other stage to create the key. get() is
+        # safe after it: this single-writer key is overwritten, never deleted.
+        if not self.store.check([FEEDBACK_KEY]):
+            return
+        payload = json.loads(self.store.get(FEEDBACK_KEY))
+        if payload["sequence"] > self._remote_sequence:
+            self._remote_sequence = payload["sequence"]
+            self._last_remote_update = monotonic()
+            self.consumed_batch_id = payload["consumed_batch_id"]
+            self._remote_samples = [
+                PPStageSample(**sample) for sample in payload["samples"]
+            ]
+
+    @property
+    def queue_depth(self) -> int:
+        # A newer consumer credit can race the local producer event query.
+        return max(0, self.ready_batch_id - self.consumed_batch_id)
+
+    @property
+    def fresh(self) -> bool:
+        return (
+            self._last_remote_update is not None
+            and monotonic() - self._last_remote_update <= self.timeout_seconds
+        )
+
+    def take_samples(self) -> list[PPBalanceSample]:
+        local = {sample.batch_id: sample for sample in self._samples}
+        paired = []
+        for remote in self._remote_samples:
+            if (
+                remote.batch_id <= self._last_paired_batch
+                or remote.batch_id not in local
+            ):
+                continue
+            producer = local[remote.batch_id]
+            if (
+                producer.boundary,
+                producer.version,
+                producer.num_tokens,
+                producer.num_reqs,
+            ) != (
+                remote.boundary,
+                remote.version,
+                remote.num_tokens,
+                remote.num_reqs,
+            ):

+                    "Dynamic PP stage feedback does not match its batch header/workload"
+                )
+            paired.append(
+                PPBalanceSample(
+                    producer.batch_id,
+                    producer.boundary,
+                    producer.version,
+                    producer.num_tokens,
+                    producer.num_reqs,
+                    producer.elapsed_ms,
+                    remote.elapsed_ms,
+                )
+            )
+            self._last_paired_batch = remote.batch_id
+            self.num_paired_samples += 1
+        return paired
+
+    def stats(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        return {
+            "ready_queue_depth": self.queue_depth if self.pp_rank == 0 else None,
+            "ready_batch_id": self.ready_batch_id if self.pp_rank == 0 else None,
+            "consumed_batch_id": self.consumed_batch_id,
+            "feedback_fresh": self.fresh if self.pp_rank == 0 else None,
+            "feedback_age_seconds": round(monotonic() - self._last_remote_update, 3)
+            if self._last_remote_update is not None
+            else None,
+            "completed_timing_samples": len(self._samples),
+            "paired_timing_samples": self.num_paired_samples,
+            "pending_device_events": len(self._steps),
+        }

+"""Registered PP cache writes using MooncakeConnector's memory operations."""
+
+from collections.abc import Callable, Mapping
+from typing import Any
+
+from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.mooncake.transfer_engine import (
+    batch_write,
+    create_transfer_engine,
+    register_memory,
+    unregister_memory,
+)
+from vllm.utils.network_utils import get_ip
+
+
+class PPMooncakeTransport:
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        state: Mapping,
+        device_module: Any,
+        protocol: str,
+        device_name: str,
+        engine_factory: Callable[[], Any] | None = None,
+    ):
+        self.state = state
+        self.regions = [
+            (layer, key, raw.data_ptr(), raw.nbytes)
+            for layer in sorted(state)
+            for key, raw in sorted(state[layer].items())
+        ]
+        self.addresses = [region[2] for region in self.regions]
+        sizes = [region[3] for region in self.regions]
+        self.registered_bytes = sum(sizes)
+        self._closed = False
+        self._peer_regions: dict[tuple[int, str], int] = {}
+        self._peer_session: str | None = None
+        hostname = get_ip()
+        device = next(iter(next(iter(state.values())).values())).device
+        try:
+            self.engine = create_transfer_engine(
+                hostname, protocol, device_name, engine_factory=engine_factory
+            )
+        finally:
+            # NVLink engine initialization may change the calling thread's device.
+            if device.type != "cpu":
+                device_module.set_device(device)
+        port = self.engine.get_rpc_port()
+        if type(port) is not int or not 0 < port < 65536:
+            raise ValueError("Mooncake did not provide a valid RPC port")
+        self.session = f"{hostname}:{port}"
+        register_memory(self.engine, self.addresses, sizes)
+
+    def bind_peer(self, session: str, regions: list) -> None:
+        expected = {(layer, key): size for layer, key, _, size in self.regions}
+        actual = {}
+        addresses = {}
+        for layer, key, address, size in regions:
+            if type(address) is not int or address <= 0 or (layer, key) in actual:
+                raise ValueError("Invalid Mooncake peer cache region")
+            actual[layer, key] = size
+            addresses[layer, key] = address
+        if actual != expected or not isinstance(session, str) or not session:
+            raise ValueError("Mooncake peer cache regions differ")
+        self._peer_regions, self._peer_session = addresses, session
+
+    def write(self, layers: list[int], max_chunk_bytes: int) -> None:
+        if self._closed or self._peer_session is None:
+            raise RuntimeError("Mooncake PP transport is closed or has no peer")
+        sources, targets, sizes = [], [], []
+        for layer in layers:
+            for key, raw in sorted(self.state[layer].items()):
+                target = self._peer_regions[layer, key]
+                for start in range(0, raw.nbytes, max_chunk_bytes):
+                    sources.append(raw.data_ptr() + start)
+                    targets.append(target + start)
+                    sizes.append(min(raw.nbytes - start, max_chunk_bytes))
+        ret = batch_write(self.engine, self._peer_session, sources, targets, sizes)
+        if ret != 0:
+            raise RuntimeError(f"Mooncake PP cache write failed (ret={ret})")
+
+    def close(self) -> None:
+        if self._closed:
+            return
+        unregister_memory(self.engine, self.addresses)
+        self._closed = True
+        # Keep tensors alive until after the engine releases its registrations.
+        self.engine = None

+"""Publish PP ownership epochs and transfer each changed layer's cache backing."""
+
+import json
+import time
+from collections.abc import Callable, Mapping
+from typing import Any

+import torch
+import torch.distributed as dist

+from vllm.v1.worker.pp.boundary import PPBoundary

+CONTROL_KEY_PREFIX = "vllm_dynamic_pp_control/"
+STATE_TRANSFER_CHUNK_BYTES = 256 * 1024 * 1024
+
+
+class PPControlChannel:
+    """One producer and consumer on TP0 of the same PP CPU-group store.
+
+    The producer must acquire its bounded activation-send slot before send().
+    The consumer reads the header before posting that batch's activation receive,
+    so completed activation sends also bound unconsumed control keys. Each new
+    group store starts at batch zero; successful receives delete their keys.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, store: Any):
+        self.store = store
+        self._sent: PPBoundary | None = None
+        self._received: PPBoundary | None = None
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _validate(header: PPBoundary, previous: PPBoundary | None) -> None:
+        if not isinstance(header, PPBoundary):
+            raise ValueError("PP control requires a boundary header")
+        PPBoundary.from_wire(header.to_wire())
+        expected_batch = 0 if previous is None else previous.batch_id + 1
+        if header.batch_id != expected_batch or header.boundary <= 0:
+            raise ValueError("PP control batch is out of order or boundary is invalid")
+        if previous is not None and (
+            header.version < previous.version
+            or header.version == previous.version
+            and header.boundary != previous.boundary
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("PP control boundary version is inconsistent")
+
+    def send(self, header: PPBoundary) -> None:
+        """Publish one immutable batch header without waiting for its consumer."""
+        self._validate(header, self._sent)
+        key = f"{CONTROL_KEY_PREFIX}{header.batch_id}"
+        if self.store.check([key]):
+            raise ValueError("PP control batch header was already published")
+        self.store.set(key, json.dumps(header.to_wire()))
+        self._sent = header
+
+    def receive(self, expected_batch_id: int) -> PPBoundary:
+        """Read the next batch's header, validate its epoch, then remove its key."""
+        next_batch = 0 if self._received is None else self._received.batch_id + 1
+        if type(expected_batch_id) is not int or expected_batch_id != next_batch:
+            raise ValueError("PP control expected batch is out of order")
+        key = f"{CONTROL_KEY_PREFIX}{expected_batch_id}"
+        header = PPBoundary.from_wire(json.loads(self.store.get(key)))
+        if header.batch_id != expected_batch_id:
+            raise ValueError("PP control header does not match the expected batch")
+        self._validate(header, self._received)
+        if not self.store.delete_key(key):
+            raise ValueError("PP control batch header disappeared before consumption")
+        self._received = header
+        return header
+
+
+class PPStateTransfer:
+    """Both stages must call move with the same CPU-agreed boundary header.
+
+    The adapter must expose each component's entire dedicated byte storage,
+    including allocator padding. It must keep these allocations stable for the
+    lifetime of this object. Unchanged boundaries perform no device work.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        pp_group: Any,
+        device_module: Any,
+        state: Mapping,
+        *,
+        max_chunk_bytes: int = STATE_TRANSFER_CHUNK_BYTES,
+        cache_layout: Mapping | None = None,
+        backend: str = "collective",
+        mooncake_protocol: str = "rdma",
+        mooncake_device_name: str = "",
+        mooncake_engine_factory: Callable[[], Any] | None = None,
+    ):

+        self._bytes = 0
+        self._chunks = 0
+        self._seconds = 0.0

+        self._backend = backend
+        self._transport: Any = None
+        self._failed = False
+        self._closed = False

+            error = "PP cache backend must be collective or mooncake"
+        peers = self._gather(
+            {
+                "description": description,
+                "chunk_bytes": max_chunk_bytes,
+                "cache_layout": cache_layout,
+                "backend": backend,
+                "protocol": mooncake_protocol if backend == "mooncake" else None,
+                "error": error,
+            }
+        )
+        self._raise_peer_errors(peers)
+        if (
+            peers[0]["description"] != peers[1]["description"]
+            or peers[0]["chunk_bytes"] != peers[1]["chunk_bytes"]
+            or peers[0]["cache_layout"] != peers[1]["cache_layout"]
+            or peers[0]["backend"] != peers[1]["backend"]
+            or peers[0]["protocol"] != peers[1]["protocol"]
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(
+                "PP cache layer/component shape, dtype, bytes, or block layout differ"
+            )
+        self._description = description
+        self._storage = storage
+        if backend == "mooncake":
+            error = None
+            try:
+                from vllm.v1.worker.pp.mooncake import PPMooncakeTransport
+
+                self._transport = PPMooncakeTransport(
+                    state,
+                    device_module,
+                    mooncake_protocol,
+                    mooncake_device_name,
+                    mooncake_engine_factory,
+                )
+            except Exception as exc:
+                error = str(exc)
+            peers = self._gather(
+                {
+                    "error": error,
+                    "session": self._transport.session if self._transport else None,
+                    "regions": self._transport.regions if self._transport else None,
+                }
+            )
+            if any(peer["error"] is not None for peer in peers):
+                if self._transport is not None:
+                    self._transport.close()
+                self._raise_peer_errors(peers)
+            peer = peers[1 - pp_group.rank_in_group]
+            error = None
+            try:
+                self._transport.bind_peer(peer["session"], peer["regions"])
+            except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
+                error = str(exc)
+            peers = self._gather({"error": error})
+            if any(peer["error"] is not None for peer in peers):
+                self._transport.close()
+                self._raise_peer_errors(peers)
+
+    def _gather(self, value: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
+        peers: list[Any] = [None, None]
+        dist.all_gather_object(peers, value, group=self.pp.cpu_group)
+        return peers
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _raise_peer_errors(peers: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
+        errors = [
+            f"PP{rank}: {peer['error']}"
+            for rank, peer in enumerate(peers)
+            if peer["error"] is not None
+        ]
+        if errors:
+            raise ValueError("PP cache state validation failed: " + "; ".join(errors))
+
+    def _inspect(self) -> tuple[list[Any], list[Any], str | None]:
+        description, storage = [], []
+        try:
+            if (
+                type(self._max_chunk_bytes) is not int
+                or not 0 < self._max_chunk_bytes <= STATE_TRANSFER_CHUNK_BYTES
+            ):
+                raise ValueError("PP cache transfer chunk size must be in [1, 256 MiB]")
+            if not callable(getattr(self.device_module, "synchronize", None)):
+                raise ValueError("Device module has no synchronize operation")
+            if not isinstance(self.state, Mapping) or not self.state:
+                raise ValueError("Cache state must be a nonempty layer mapping")
+            if any(type(layer) is not int or layer < 0 for layer in self.state):
+                raise ValueError("Cache layer keys must be nonnegative integers")
+            allocations: set[tuple[str, int]] = set()
+            device = None
+            for layer in sorted(self.state):
+                components = self.state[layer]
+                if not isinstance(components, Mapping) or not components:
+                    raise ValueError(f"Layer {layer} has no cache component mapping")
+                if any(type(key) is not str or not key for key in components):
+                    raise ValueError("Cache component keys must be nonempty strings")
+                for key in sorted(components):
+                    raw = components[key]
+                    if not isinstance(raw, torch.Tensor):
+                        raise TypeError(f"Cache {layer}/{key} is not a tensor")
+                    if raw.dtype != torch.int8 or raw.ndim != 1:
+                        raise ValueError(
+                            f"Cache {layer}/{key} must be 1D int8 raw backing"
+                        )
+                    backing = raw.untyped_storage()
+                    if (
+                        raw.layout != torch.strided
+                        or not raw.is_contiguous()
+                        or raw.numel() == 0
+                        or raw.storage_offset() != 0
+                        or raw.nbytes != backing.nbytes()
+                    ):
+                        raise ValueError(
+                            f"Cache {layer}/{key} is not a complete raw allocation"
+                        )
+                    if device is None:
+                        device = raw.device
+                    if raw.device != device:
+                        raise ValueError("Local cache components must share one device")
+                    allocation = (str(raw.device), backing.data_ptr())
+                    if allocation in allocations:
+                        raise ValueError(
+                            f"Cache {layer}/{key} aliases another component"
+                        )
+                    allocations.add(allocation)
+                    description.append(
+                        (
+                            layer,
+                            key,
+                            tuple(raw.shape),
+                            str(raw.dtype),
+                            raw.nbytes,
+                            raw.device.type,
+                        )
+                    )
+                    storage.append((layer, key, allocation, backing.nbytes()))
+            return description, storage, None
+        except (TypeError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
+            return [], [], str(exc)
+
+    def move(self, oldcut: int, newcut: int, batch_id: int) -> None:
+        """Quiesce both stages, then copy each changed layer from its old owner."""
+        if self._failed or self._closed:
+            raise RuntimeError("PP cache transport failed or is closed; abort runtime")
+        valid_numbers = all(
+            type(value) is int and value >= 0 for value in (oldcut, newcut, batch_id)
+        )
+        if valid_numbers and oldcut == newcut:
+            if (
+                not valid_numbers
+                or batch_id <= self._last_batch
+                or self._boundary is not None
+                and self._boundary != oldcut
+            ):
+                raise ValueError("Invalid unchanged PP cache boundary/batch")
+            self._boundary, self._last_batch = newcut, batch_id
+            return
+
+        started = time.monotonic()
+        description, storage, error = self._inspect()
+        layers = (
+            list(range(min(oldcut, newcut), max(oldcut, newcut)))
+            if valid_numbers
+            else []
+        )
+        if error is None and (
+            not valid_numbers
+            or batch_id <= self._last_batch
+            or self._boundary is not None
+            and self._boundary != oldcut
+        ):
+            error = "Invalid changed PP cache boundary/batch"
+        if error is None and (
+            description != self._description or storage != self._storage
+        ):
+            error = "Cache allocations changed after validation"
+        if error is None and any(layer not in self.state for layer in layers):
+            error = "Changed boundary crosses a layer without replicated cache state"
+        peers = self._gather(
+            {
+                "oldcut": oldcut if type(oldcut) is int else None,
+                "newcut": newcut if type(newcut) is int else None,
+                "batch_id": batch_id if type(batch_id) is int else None,
+                "error": error,
+            }
+        )
+        self._raise_peer_errors(peers)
+        if any(
+            (peer["oldcut"], peer["newcut"], peer["batch_id"])
+            != (oldcut, newcut, batch_id)
+            for peer in peers
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("PP cache handoff boundary/batch differs between stages")
+
+        error = None
+        try:
+            self.device_module.synchronize()
+        except RuntimeError as exc:
+            error = str(exc)
+        self._raise_peer_errors(self._gather({"error": error}))
+
+        moved_bytes = 0
+        chunks = 0
+        for layer in layers:
+            owner = 0 if layer < oldcut else 1
+            for key in sorted(self.state[layer]):
+                raw = self.state[layer][key]
+                for start in range(0, raw.numel(), self._max_chunk_bytes):
+                    if self._transport is None:
+                        self.pp.broadcast(
+                            raw[start : start + self._max_chunk_bytes], src=owner
+                        )
+                    chunks += 1
+                moved_bytes += raw.nbytes
+        if self._transport is not None:
+            error = None
+            try:
+                owner = 0 if newcut < oldcut else 1
+                if self.pp.rank_in_group == owner:
+                    self._transport.write(layers, self._max_chunk_bytes)
+            except Exception as exc:
+                error = str(exc)
+            peers = self._gather({"error": error})
+            if any(peer["error"] is not None for peer in peers):
+                self._failed = True
+                self._raise_peer_errors(peers)
+        self.device_module.synchronize()
+        elapsed = time.monotonic() - started
+        self._boundary, self._last_batch = newcut, batch_id
+        self._moves += 1
+        self._bytes += moved_bytes
+        self._chunks += chunks
+        self._seconds += elapsed
+        self._last_move = {
+            "batch_id": batch_id,
+            "oldcut": oldcut,
+            "newcut": newcut,
+            "layers": layers,
+            "bytes": moved_bytes,
+            "chunks": chunks,
+            "seconds": elapsed,
+        }
+
+    def stats(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        last_move = (
+            self._last_move | {"layers": list(self._last_move["layers"])}
+            if self._last_move is not None
+            else None
+        )
+        return {
+            "backend": self._backend,
+            "registered_bytes": self._transport.registered_bytes
+            if self._transport is not None
+            else 0,
+            "moves": self._moves,
+            "bytes": self._bytes,
+            "chunks": self._chunks,
+            "seconds": self._seconds,
+            "last_move": last_move,
+        }
+
+    def close(self) -> None:
+        if self._closed:
+            return
+        if self._failed:
+            raise RuntimeError("Failed PP transfers retain buffers until worker exit")
+        if self._transport is not None:
+            self._transport.close()
+        self._closed = True
